notes:
Summary: Mid-market SaaS (developer productivity + in-product help). Started with Hosted API for quick integration (chat + doc search) during Q4 2025; now moving to Dedicated for predictable latency, EU data residency, and cost predictability. Procurement/legal are active — MSA/DPA redlines in play.

POC & technical notes:
- 2025-12-03: initial Hosted API POC (chat integrated in staging). Found throughput OK for low concurrency; p99 latency spikes at peak load (500 concurrent users) ~700-800ms — engineering concerned.
- 2026-01-15: SE demo of Dedicated architecture + VPC peering options (Diego). Team liked dedicated GPU pool and autoscaling knobs.
- 2026-02-28: performance POC on Dedicated (small reserved pool). Observed p50~60ms, p95~180ms, p99~270ms for typical session lengths (avg tokens 120). Meets product requirements for chat but legal wants SLA language tightened.
- Model preferences: open Llama-derivative family for embeddings/rerank; want quantized variants for cost.
- Routing: plan to route sensitive EU traffic to EU Dedicated cluster; fallback to hosted fallback only as last resort (explicit consent).

Procurement/legal details:
- Primary asks from EmberField legal: tighten data residency in DPA (explicit EU-only processing for EU customers), stronger audit logging guarantee, and KMS/HSM integration for at-rest key control.
- MSA redlines: EmberField pushed back on Redwood standard indemnity caps and wants liability carveouts for customer data breaches tied to third-party infra.
- SLA: EmberField requests p99 latency SLA (chat) <= 300ms and 99.95% availability for Dedicated cluster; Redwood SLA currently provides 99.9% and per-model latency guidance — negotiating uplift + financial credits.
- Retention: EmberField requires 90-day dev/test log retention and 1-year audit log retention for compliance audits.
- Security attestation: SOC2 Type II report acceptable; EmberField also asked for ISO27001 evidence and to run a short on-site questionnaire (security spreadsheet in drive).

Commercial/pricing:
- EmberField expects to commit to a monthly reserved capacity (3x A100-equivalent slots) with burst credits. Target ARR range $120k-$300k depending on final commit and discount.
- Billing ask: quarterly invoicing with PO number and ability to wire; wants a committed-rate break after 6 months.

Timeline & next steps:
- 2026-03-04: Redwood sent redline response to EmberField legal (drive:contracts/emberfield_msa_redline_20260304.docx).
- EmberField legal to return counters by 2026-03-18. (Next step: finalize MSA/DPA.)
- SE to schedule Dedicated onboarding + network design call week of 2026-03-22 (tasks: VPC CIDR allocation, peering windows, traffic routing policy).
- Security review: EmberField to finish questionnaire and confirm SOC2/ISO docs by 2026-03-25.

Quotes from stakeholders:
- Product lead: "We need deterministic latency for in-product assistant — cannot slip during rollout to 100k users."
- Legal: "Data residency and indemnity are deal-breakers unless we get explicit language."

Open action items (owner in brackets):
- Finalize MSA/DPA redline resolution (Legal / Samira).
- Technical onboarding checklist for Dedicated (SE: Diego) — network diagrams + KMS integration plan.
- Pricing appendix for committed capacity + credits (Sales Ops).
- Provide ISO27001 evidence and expanded SOC2 controls mapping (Security).

Notes & tone: shorthand in threads, some repeated asks across calls. EmberField is close to signing once legal items are resolved — primary friction remains indemnity/sla and data residency. Procurement wants everything complete before end of April 2026 to align with budgeting cycle.
